course_description:
This course involves 400-480 hours of industry experience, through a work integrated learning (WIL) placement in a production or service enterprise. It provides students with the opportunity to apply the theoretical knowledge and research skills they have developed earlier in the Master of Food Science and Technology program in a real-world industry setting.

Through this immersive experience, students will gain a deeper understanding of industry operations, expectations, and professional standards, enhancing their career readiness and employability.

Please note the following important conditions:

Information about enrolling in a placement course, including registering your interest and application deadlines, can be found here: science.uq.edu.au/placements . Eligible students will apply for UQ-sourced placement opportunities in a competitive selection process.

This course offers students practical, industry-based experience and the opportunity to strengthen professional skills in a real-world setting. It bridges theory and practice by allowing students to apply their theoretical concepts and knowledge, while understanding industry operations before graduation.

Students will complete 400-480 hours of placement in an enterprise such as a food production company or a food certification or food safety authority (e.g. Safe Food Queensland). While your placement schedule should comfortably allow you to meet the minimum requirement of 400 hours, acceptance of a placement constitutes a commitment to the full agreed period. Students are required to remain in their placement from the confirmed start date through to the nominated end date, as recorded by Science Industry Placements, and must not cease attendance upon reaching the minimum hours . This ensures continuity for the host organisation and maximises your professional learning experience.

This placement is organised by Science Industry Placements. Students should be mindful that UQ Industry Partners make decisions about which student/s will be offered a placement with their organisation. This is a competitive process. Once the student accepts a placement opportunity organised with an industry host partner, the student cannot withdraw from the offer and drop their course enrolment , unless due to extenuating circumstances which will need to be presented to and discussed with the Course Coordinator. The Course Coordinator will deal with these issues on a case-by-case basis.

In addition to the workplace requirements, students will attend compulsory orientation and employability workshops before and after the placement, learning the importance of self-reflection in their personal and professional development, and improving their ability to articulate their skills and experiences to potential employers.

The host organisation will appoint a Placement Supervisor for each student. The Course Coordinator acts as the Academic Supervisor and is available to resolve issues that arise during the placement, as well as discuss progress with the Placement Supervisor and the student.

Industry placements are generally unpaid. Please be aware UQ insurance coverage applies to unpaid placements. If the student is paid, the company is required to insure the student.

During the placement, students will adhere to the UQ Student Charter (https://ppl.app.uq.edu.au/content/3.60.01-student-charter) and the UQ Placements in Coursework Programs Policy (https://ppl.app.uq.edu.au/content/3.10.04-placements-coursework-programs), as well as act in accordance with host organisation’s policies, procedures and regulations. Students may be asked to enter into a confidentiality and intellectual property agreement with the host organisation. Students should seek their own independent legal advice to ensure they are aware of their obligations and before signing such agreements. The UQ Union (https://www.uqu.com.au/student-support/legal) offers a free legal service to all UQ Students who are currently enrolled.

For student administrative matters relating to this course, please email agriculture@enquire.uq.edu.au (http://enquire.uq.edu.au) (mailto:agriculture@enquire.uq.edu.au) or phone 3365 1171.

At the School of Agriculture and Food Sustainability, we are committed to creating an inclusive and empowering learning environment for all students. We value and respect the diverse range of experiences our students bring to their education, and we believe that this diversity is crucial for fostering a rich culture of knowledge-sharing and meaningful exploration. We hold students and staff accountable for actively contributing to establishing a respectful and supportive learning environment.

Bullying, harassment, and discrimination in any form are strictly against our principles and againstﾠ UQ Policy, ﾠand will not be tolerated. If you have any concerns about your experience in this course, we encourage you to tell a member of the course teaching team. Your well-being and a positive learning atmosphere are of utmost importance to us.

assessment_details.title: Compulsory Orientation Workshop & Quiz (In-class, Online)
assessment_details.other_conditions: Work integrated learning, Secure. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: This full-day compulsory orientation workshop is designed to prepare students for their 13-week industry placement with food industry host providers across south-east Queensland. The session will equip students with critical information, resources and expectations to ensure a successful and professional placement experience. By the end of the workshop, students will: Gain insights into workplace culture, professional communication, and employer expectations in the Australian food industry. Develop an awareness of workplace health and safety. Learn strategies for adapting to new work environments and building professional relationships. At the conclusion of the full-day compulsory workshop, students attempt a timed online quiz. The quiz will be based on the workshop content. Duration: 20 minutes Marks: 20 marks Attempts: One attempt only Question types: Multiple choice, true/false, short answer scenario-based questions. Further details are available on the FOOD7021 Learn.UQ Ultra site. This test will be taken on a UQ campus location with secure internet service. Please bring your own device for this Quiz and ensure that it is fully charged . Loan laptops may be available from the UQ Library. This assessment task is to be completed in-person. The use of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) or Machine Translation (MT) tools will not be permitted. Any attempted use of AI or MT may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct. Read full task description Hide full task description

By completing this task, you will: Critically analyse feedback from your industry host supervisor. Identify key strengths and areas for growth. Develop a structured plan for improving technical, professional, and communication skills. Align your personal development with industry expectations and career goals. assessment_details.title: Supervisor Report 1
assessment_details.other_conditions: Work integrated learning, Secure. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: Purpose: The Placement Supervisor will assess the student’s progress, performance and conduct approximately three weeks after placement begins . This feedback helps identify development opportunities for the remainder of the placement. Industry Placement Supervisor Responsibilities: The assessment request is automatically sent to the industry placement supervisor, granting access to complete the Supervisor Report 1 in InPlace. The placement supervisor is encouraged to use the report as an opportunity to conduct a formal performance review session with the student and provide face-to-face feedback before submitting the report electronically. Further information can be found in the FOOD7021 Learn.UQ Ultra site. The Supervisor Report must be submitted by the due date by the industry placement supervisor or their authorised representative. Students who achieve 'Unsatisfactory' in any of the five evaluated areas, OR receives an overall mark of 50% or less, will have their placement paused. They will be referred to the Course Coordinator and required to attend a feedback and academic progression outcomes meeting. The student will need to implement a one-week performance plan. The Placement Supervisor will be asked to report again at the week's end, and if performance is still unsatisfactory, the student's placement will be terminated and they will have to withdraw from the course. Further information can be found in the FOOD7021 Learn.UQ Ultra site. Read full task description Hide full task description

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 1 To Week 12 (27 Jul - 25 Oct)
learning_activities.topic: Professional Experience Students undertake 400-480 hours of workplace experience in a host organisation under the supervision of the Placement Supervisor. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04

Orientation Workshop This activity will take place in-person on the first day of semester. Attendance is compulsory. The orientation session will be specific to FOOD7021, covering professionalism, the course requirements and discussing assessment expectations and submission requirements. Learning outcomes: L01

Employability Workshop The post-placement Employability Workshop is held during Teaching Week 13 of semester. Attendance is compulsory. This will be an in-person activity, where students will have the opportunity to unpack their recent work integrated learning experience and articulate the employability. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04
